_meta.indication: Treatment of severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents 12 years and older

pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 12 years of age and older with alopecia areata and >=50% scalp hair loss, including alopecia totalis and alopecia universalis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Response based on an absolute SALT score <=20 at Week 24
pivotal_trials.n: N=718 randomized (recommended 50 mg dose arm N=130 vs placebo N=131 in primary analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: SALT <=20 response at Week 24: 23.0% ritlecitinib 50 mg vs 1.6% placebo; difference from placebo 21.4 (95% CI 13.4, 29.5); p<0.00001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=1%) include headache (10.8% vs 8.5% placebo), diarrhea (10.0% vs 3.8%), acne (6.2% vs 4.7%), rash, urticaria, folliculitis, pyrexia, atopic dermatitis, dizziness, blood CPK increased, herpes zoster, red blood cell count decreased, and stomatitis. Serious risks include serious infections (12 subjects, 0.66 per 100 subject-years), malignancy, herpes zoster, and thromboembolic events.
target_moa: Ritlecitinib is a kinase inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits Janus kinase 3 (JAK3) and the TEC (tyrosine kinase expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma) kinase family (BMX, BTK, ITK, TEC, TXK), without clinically relevant activity at JAK1, JAK2, or TYK2

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and thrombosis (JAK inhibitor class warnings)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held because no unexpected significant safety, efficacy, or controversial issues were identified

basis.text: Application was reviewed under standard (not priority) review

summary.text: Ritlecitinib was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity, received a Breakthrough Therapy Designation on 7/31/2018, and was reviewed under standard review; it was approved without accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The applicant submitted a 505(b)(1) application for LITFULO (ritlecitinib) tablets for the treatment of alopecia areata. Ritlecitinib is a new molecular entity kinase inhibitor.

requirement.text: 4463-1: Conduct the open-label long-term extension (LTE) study to evaluate the safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric subjects 6 to <12 years of age with moderate to severe alopecia areata who completed studies B7981031 or B7981027

citations.quote: **4463-1** Conduct the open-label long-term extension (LTE) study to evaluate the safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric subjects 6 to <12 years of age with moderate to severe alopecia areata who have completed previous ritlecitinib studies B7981031 or B7981027 and are eligible to receive ritlecitinib.

requirement.text: 4463-2: Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to investigate the safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric subjects (6 to <12 years of age) with moderate to severe AA (SALT score of 50 or greater)

citations.quote: **4463-2** Conduct a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to investigate the safety of ritelcitinib in pediatric subjects (6 to <12 years of age) with moderate to severe AA (defined by \ge 50\% scalp hair loss, measured by a SALT score of 50 or greater).

requirement.text: 4463-3: Submit the final study report for a PK study comparing systemic exposures in adults and adolescents to pediatric subjects ages 6 to <12 years with moderate to severe AA (at least 12 evaluable subjects)

citations.quote: **4463-3** Submit the final study report for a PK study which aims to compare the systemic exposures of the dose/regimen in adults and adolescents to that of pediatric subjects ages 6 to <12 years with moderate to severe alopecia areata. Provide data on at least 12 evaluable subjects.

requirement.text: 4463-4: Submit the final study report for an ongoing open-label long-term study to investigate the safety of ritlecitinib in adults and adolescents with AA (12 years of age and older)

citations.quote: **4463-4** Submit the final study report for an ongoing open-label long-term study to investigate the safety of ritelcitinib in adults and adolescents with AA (12 years of age and older).

requirement.text: 4463-5: Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with alopecia areata exposed to ritlecitinib during pregnancy with unexposed comparators

citations.quote: **4463-5** Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry, preferably a disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry, using a cohort analysis that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with alopecia areata exposed to ritelcitinib during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s).

requirement.text: 4463-6: Conduct an additional pregnancy study using a different design (e.g., retrospective cohort or case control) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small-for-gestational-age, and preterm birth in women exposed to ritlecitinib during pregnancy

citations.quote: **4463-6** Conduct an additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the pregnancy exposure registry (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to rifecitibin during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.
